source_spans.locator: Nature Reviews Neuroscience 8, published pp.976-977, opening theoretical contrast: modality-specific content is necessary but not sufficient; cross-concept generalization motivates an additional shared convergence system

same article, published p.977, Figure 1 and caption: compared cortical architectures, modality-specific regions and connections, shared convergence system, task-dependent routing, and common task-independent processing

same article, published p.977, architecture-specific lesion prediction: damage to the shared system should yield input- and output-modality-independent impairment, whereas no focal lesion is expected to do so under the alternative architecture

same article, published pp.978-981, acquired-disorder evidence: semantic dementia shows selective but generalized impairment across reception/expression modalities and concept classes together with relatively focal bilateral anterior-temporal degeneration; evidential caveats are discussed

same article, published pp.983-985, computational rationale: convergent architectures process different information types through a common population and better learn conceptual similarity relations than task-gated pathways

same article, published p.987, concluding synthesis: generalized degradation covaries with focal bilateral anterior-temporal degeneration and cross-modal access/generalization abilities are attributed to this system

institutions: MRC Cognition and Brain Sciences Unit

conditions: a cortical architecture is required to support meaning-related generalization and access across sensory, motor, and linguistic channels
substrate: widely distributed modality-specific cortical regions and a candidate shared bilateral anterior-temporal convergence system
task: receive information in one channel and express related information in another
generalize across entities that are related in meaning despite differing modality-specific features

nodes.description: widely distributed cortical regions carrying sensory, motor, and linguistic feature information
shared convergence system through which multiple modality-specific representations interact, proposed to be implemented in bilateral anterior temporal cortex
ability to integrate across input and output channels and to generalize among meaning-related entities whose specific features differ
candidate architecture in which distributed modality-specific regions and their direct connections constitute the complete cortical network for the target functions
candidate architecture containing the distributed modality-specific system plus a common convergence stage used across modalities, categories, and tasks
relatively focal degeneration or damage affecting the proposed shared convergence system
selective but broad impairment that is expressed across input modalities, output modalities, and multiple classes of items

relations.description: the reviewed account treats distributed modality-specific information as necessary but insufficient and additionally requires a shared convergence system for cross-channel integration and generalization
the two compared architectures differ in whether a common convergence stage supplements direct connections among modality-specific regions
the shared-convergence account predicts that relatively focal damage to the common system can produce impairment that generalizes across reception and expression channels and across item classes
the convergent architecture is predicted to support learning and use of similarity relations that cut across modality-specific feature differences
